property_summary: For any interfaceId input, the reference contract's supportsInterface returns true whenever the id equals IERC1155 or IERC1155MetadataURI (or their combination), but the mutant returns false for those ids — so calling supportsInterface with either of those interface IDs must yield true on the reference and may be false on the mutant.

For every bytes4 interfaceId input, the reference contract's supportsInterface returns true when interfaceId equals the IERC1155 or IERC1155MetadataURI interface id (or their combination), whereas the mutant always returns false for those ids — so there exists an interfaceId (the IERC1155 id) for which reference returns true but mutant returns false.

For any bytes4 iface id the reference C.supportsInterface returns true when asked about IERC1155 or IERC1155MetadataURI ids (i.e. it reports support for the ERC1155 interfaces); the mutant breaks this by returning false for those interface ids — so there exists an iface id (fuzzable) for which reference returns true but the mutant may return false.

For every bytes4 interfaceId, the reference C.supportsInterface(interfaceId) returns true whenever interfaceId equals IERC1155 or IERC1155MetadataURI; the mutant removes those disjuncts so there exist interfaceIds (specifically those ERC1155 IDs) where the reference returns true but the mutant returns false.

For every bytes4 interfaceId, the reference C.supportsInterface(interfaceId) returns true whenever the id equals IERC1155 or IERC1155MetadataURI; the mutant removes those checks so there exists at least one interfaceId (the IERC1155 or IERC1155MetadataURI id) for which the reference returns true but the mutant returns false — the test fuzzes an interfaceId and asserts that if C reports support for that id then that id must equal either IERC1155 or IERC1155MetadataURI (a property the reference satisfies for all inputs but the mutant violates for some inputs).

For any account and token id within the valid range, balanceOf(account, id) returns the stored balance for that exact id in the contract's ledger; the mutant returns the balance for id+1 instead, so for many ids the values differ.

For any account and token id, C.balanceOf(account,id) returns the stored balance for that exact id (i.e. reading _balances[id][account]); the mutant returns _balances[id+1][account], so there exist ids for which the returned value differs (the property: balanceOf(account,id) equals getAllowanceRemaining/other? — instead we assert consistency with mint then balanceOf), causing the mutant to fail when querying an id that was minted (since it will read next id).

For any account and tokenId, if the contract mints `quantity` of tokenId to the account, then a subsequent balanceOf(account, tokenId) equals that minted quantity; the mutant that reads _balances[id+1] will return a different value for at least some tokenId (failing this equality).

For any account and token id, if the contract mints a specific quantity of that tokenId to the account then balanceOf(account, tokenId) returns that minted quantity; the mutant reading _balances[id+1] will return a different value for at least some minted tokenId and so will violate this equality.

For any account and token id, if we mint only to that id and ensure the adjacent id (id+1) has zero balance for that account, then balanceOf(account, id) returns the minted amount; the mutant that reads id+1 will return zero instead, so the equality is violated for those inputs.

For any non-zero account and any token id, balanceOf(account,id) in the correct contract equals the stored balances mapping (i.e. can be non-zero when tokens were minted to that account); the mutant always returns 0 so there exist inputs (an account and id after minting) where mutant's balanceOf differs.

For any account and token id, if the contract has a nonzero stored balance for that (account,id) (e.g. after minting to that account), then balanceOf(account,id) returns that stored (nonzero) balance; the mutant always returns 0 and therefore will disagree when a positive balance exists.

For any account and token id, if the contract has a nonzero stored ERC1155 balance for that (account,id) (e.g. after minting), balanceOf(account,id) returns a positive (nonzero) value; the mutant always returns zero and thus will disagree for some inputs where a mint made the stored balance > 0.

For any account and tokenId, calling getAllowanceRemaining(owner, tokenId) returns a value equal to the stored allowanceRemaining (or the daily allowance if replenished) and thus is non-negative; the mutant that forces balanceOf to always return 0 does not affect getAllowanceRemaining on the reference but can cause behavior differences in mint() which depends on neuron.balanceOf(msg.sender) > price — the property asserts that after minting tokens to an account, balanceOf(account, tokenId) > 0 (reference) so getAllowanceRemaining remains readable and non-reverting; the mutant will make balanceOf return 0 causing the same sequence to fail and thus the assertion distinguishing them will fail for some fuzz inputs.

For any account and tokenId, after C.mint(tokenId, quantity) succeeds (so the contract stored a positive balance for that account & id), calling balanceOf(account, tokenId) returns a positive (nonzero) value in the reference; the mutant that always returns 0 will violate this for some fuzzed inputs (account, tokenId, quantity).

For any account and token id, balanceOf must return the actual stored balance _balances[id][account] (i.e. not be multiplied); the mutant that returns double the stored balance will therefore produce a different numeric result for some inputs.

For every account and token id, C.balanceOf(account,id) returns the stored uint256 balance _balances[id][account]; the mutant that returns twice the stored balance violates this numeric equality for any account/id with a nonzero stored balance.

For every account and tokenId, calling C.balanceOf(account, tokenId) returns a value equal to the actual on-chain stored token balance (i.e. the value returned is exactly the amount that previous mints/transfers set); the mutant that multiplies the stored balance by 2 will cause balanceOf to return a value different from the real stored balance for some account/tokenId (e.g., any account/tokenId with a nonzero balance).
